headline: 30 Bangladeshis return home after release from Cambodia detention centre
summary: The men were lured by brokers to Cambodia for high-paying jobs but were forced into cyber scamming and faced torture during their detention.
details: Thirty Bangladeshi nationals have returned to Dhaka on Tuesday after being released from an immigration detention centre in Cambodia.
The group arrived at the airport via a Thai Airways flight following efforts by the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment.
The ordeal began on September 3, when 32 Bangladeshis were detained by immigration police at Phnom Penh airport while attempting to return home.
While two individuals were released shortly after, the remaining 30 were held in the detention centre.
According to sources, the men were lured to Cambodia by brokers promising attractive salaries for employment.
Once there, many were forced to work in cyber scamming and online fraud operations.
The victims reported being subjected to torture when they attempted to escape from these scamming centres.
The repatriation process was accelerated after Jamuna Television broadcast a report on their situation on October 14.
caption:
Lured by promises of high pay, 30 Bangladeshis were forced into cyber scamming and tortured in Cambodia.

Thirty Bangladeshi nationals have returned to Dhaka on Tuesday after being released from an immigration detention centre in Cambodia.

The group arrived at the airport via a Thai Airways flight following efforts by the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment.

The ordeal began on September 3, when 32 Bangladeshis were detained by immigration police at Phnom Penh airport while attempting to return home.

While two individuals were released shortly after, the remaining 30 were held in the detention centre.

According to sources, the men were lured to Cambodia by brokers promising attractive salaries for employment.

Once there, many were forced to work in cyber scamming and online fraud operations.

The victims reported being subjected to torture when they attempted to escape from these scamming centres.

The repatriation process was accelerated after Jamuna Television broadcast a report on their situation on October 14.

headline_marked: 12 killed as [[bus crashes into sand-laden truck]] in Natore
headline: 12 killed as bus crashes into sand-laden truck in Natore
summary: Five traders from Shariatpur were among the deceased in the head-on collision on the Pabna-Natore highway near Bonpara.
details: A head-on collision between a bus and a sand-laden truck left 12 people dead and several others injured on the Pabna-Natore highway near Bonpara today.
Among the victims were five traders from Kazirhat Bazar in Shariatpur's Zajira upazila, who were traveling to Rajshahi to purchase agricultural produce and seeds for the Rabi season.
The deceased traders have been identified as Jewel Madbar (40), Salal Mollya (46), Sohag Shikdar (30), Samad Fakir (70), and Shahin Bepari (32).
The group had set off yesterday evening, traveling from the Naodoba roundabout near the Padma Bridge South Plaza to Bhanga bus stand before boarding a bus for Rajshahi.
The crash occurred around 4:10 am today near the Bonpara roundabout, just before the bus reached its destination.

Barkandi Union Parishad Chairman Md Lutfor Rahman and Zajira Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Al Imran stated that the administration is coordinating to bring the bodies back to Shariatpur for funeral prayers.
Two other traders from the same group, Alamgir Madbar and Faisal, survived the accident.
